latest.title: Iga Swiatek takes swing at critics after ending title drought in Cincinnati
latest.summary: Pole wins her first title in 11 months ‘Sometimes we need to fight things we shouldn’t’ It came as no surprise that almost a year of pent-up emotion exploded from Iga Swiatek the moment she slotted her final backhand winner to clinch the Canadian Open title by defeating Elena Rybakina in two clean sets on Thursday night. As she screamed towards her team members on her corner of the court, pointed to her head and furiously pumped her fist, though, it was the tenor of Swiatek’s emotion that made her reaction noteworthy: she was angry. Her anger, she explained later, stemmed from the doubtful, disapproving voices she has heard throughout these difficult periods, most of it coming from viewers and the media alike in Poland. Sports.title: Europe’s top clubs threatened Club World Cup boycott before Fifa plan collapsed

In a letter to the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, seen by the Guardian, the influential European Football Clubs (EFC) group warned its cooperation with future tournaments would hinge on Infantino backing down. It said the threat will hold unless a joint venture between EFC and Fifa – a framework for which has already been agreed – is completed before television rights can be sold for the 2028 Women’s Club World Cup. Culture.title: Kristen Schaal: The Legend of Crystal Shell review – flighty Conchords comic is still kooking on gas
Culture.summary: Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh As a half-horse half-woman who dreams of being a unicorn and performing Swan Lake, Schaal sheds little light but has plenty of sparkle For a happy handful of years in the noughties, around the time she made her TV name on Flight of the Conchords ’ sitcom, Kristen Schaal was a fringe fixture, award-nominated in 2008 for her two-hander with Kurt Braunohler, Double Down Hearts . If those shows found Schaal kooking on gas, about as wilfully dotty and insubstantial as you’d ever wish comedy to be, the intervening two decades seem to have changed her not a jot. The Legend of Crystal Shell, her two-hander with John Roberts, casts the comic actor as a half-woman, half-horse, overcoming a lifetime of shame to deliver a performance of Tchaikovsky’s Swan Lake for tonight’s audience. It plays as if written by a primary schoolchild high on pick’n’mix, and is endearing and nonplussing in equal measure. Continue reading...
